shadows.name: focus-ring

Website: outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px on every focusable part (3px on actions, pills, and tabs; inset on the photo reel), drawn by one :where(.site-root) :focus-visible rule in the utilities layer so outline-none cannot blank it. --focus is inherited per field: var(--color-club-ink) on .site-root and on white cards inside dark fields, var(--color-club-ball) on .pm-dark, #fff on .pm-halftone (Club Green).
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on every control. App: ink on the canvas, lime in the dark zone. Website: Club Ink on the white and Ball Lime fields and on white cards, Ball Lime on Deep Green, Jersey Blue, and Club Ink, white on Club Green (3.5:1; Ball Lime would read about 2.5:1 there). narrative.overview:
CoachMan is a calm, premium CRM for courts. Every app screen splits into two zones: a black command panel that holds navigation and the live list (today's sessions, the client worklist, who owes), and a soft-gray daylight canvas where the selected session or client opens as rounded white cards. Lime is the single signal across both zones. It lights whatever is live, selected, or the next action, so a coach glancing at a phone between games finds "now" without reading.

Headings and figures are large and light; everything a coach acts on is regular or medium weight and at least 36px tall, mostly 44px or more. Status speaks in soft pastel pills that always carry ink text. Depth is tonal (gray canvas, a lighter folder panel, white cards), and shadows appear only on things that float. Containers take generous 22–32px corners, and every control is a pill or a circle. People appear as initials on soft tints unless the coach uploads a photo. There is no stock or illustrative imagery, and in the app the lime BallMark is the only sport motif.

The visual authority is a reference the user pinned: the Dribbble shot "Microsoft Dynamics CRM – Lead Relationship Management Platform" by Jack R. for RonDesignLab, translated from sales to coaching. It replaced a themed "Court Lines" build and a plain "clean and light" plan, both rejected; the system refuses flat admin tables and sport-themed costume. Where the reference sets white text on pastel pills, CoachMan sets ink, because task surfaces have to read in outdoor sun.

The academy release carries the same world to the people around the coaches. The **family portal** is the calm register: the command panel becomes a black header block that holds the academy's own logo tile and name, the page title, and (on laptops) the navigation as pills; the work sits on the gray canvas as white cards, with lime spent on one thing per screen (the next session, the amount due). The **enrollment wizard** is an Operate flow in the academy's frame: the dark panel holds the academy, the tier, and the steps; one white card holds one question. The **rates sheet** prints the live catalog as a plain letterhead document. In these surfaces an academy brings only its name, logo, words, and photos (its team's portraits, a cover, and its own court photos); the CoachMan palette is never recolored for it.

The **academy website** (`/a/<slug>`: the landing page, Enroll now, and Meet the team inside one site frame) is not a CoachMan screen. It is the academy's own public face, for families and players deciding whether to train there, and the owner gave it its own identity (2026-11-07), choosing the **Pubmat** from four mocked directions: the site is set like the enrollment pubmat Filipino families already stop scrolling for, and CoachMan appears on it only as a small "Made with CoachMan" in the footer. Every section is one full-bleed field of flat color in the club's colors, sampled from the first academy's own banner and jersey: Club Green under print-dot halftone, Jersey Blue, Deep Green, Ball Lime, white, and a Club Ink footer. Archivo sets all of it: the academy's name, titles, schedules, and prices in extra-condensed black italic caps, everything else at normal width. Stickers with a white die-cut edge, photos stuck on with a white border and a slight turn, schedules on strips laid across at an angle, and a slanted Ball Lime Enroll now carry the page. Every word, photo, and figure comes from the academy's own data, and a section with nothing yet says what's coming instead of falling silent. It refuses the sports-academy template (a dark full-bleed hero photo with a centered slogan, three icon features, plan columns, a testimonial carousel) and the quiet cream-and-serif page it replaced. Its tokens and rules hold inside the website (`.site-root`) only, and the two worlds don't mix: the staff app, the family portal, the wizard, and the rates sheet the website links to keep the system above, and the website shares only CoachMan's BallMark, in its footer credit.
keyCharacteristics: Two zones: a black command panel (icon rail plus list column) beside a soft-gray canvas of white cards.
Lime marks live, selected, and primary, and nothing else.
Figtree throughout the app: light (300) for headings and figures, tabular numerals for every compared number.
Pastel status pills with ink text, never white.
Tonal depth; shadows only on floating layers.
22–32px container corners; pills and circles for every control.
Records open into fused folder tabs over a lighter panel, with lavender and lime bentos beside them.
Touch-first sizing: 44px controls, 48px check-in circles, 52px action circles.

One app world for three audiences: staff (command panel), families (black header block), and applicants (wizard frame). Visitors get the academy's own website, a separate world: an enrollment pubmat in the club's colors, set in Archivo caps.
A visible keyboard focus everywhere: in the app a 2px ring at 2px offset, ink on the canvas, lime in the dark zone; on the website a 3px ring at 3px offset.

rules.name: The Lime Is Now Rule
rules.body: Lime marks what is live, selected, or the primary action: the active rail circle, the selected tile, the action circles, the checked-in toggle, the primary bento. It never labels a category, a tag, or a chart series; categories take the pastels.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Pastel Rule
rules.body: Every lime and pastel fill carries ink (#111111) text and icons, never white. This is a deliberate accessibility deviation from the reference, whose pills set white on pastel: white on Owes Coral reads at about 2.8:1, ink at about 6.8:1.

rules.name: The Connection Color Rule
rules.body: Sync Orange speaks only about connection state (offline, syncing, a change waiting to sync), and nothing else wears it.

rules.name: The One Lime Block Rule
rules.body: A screen holds at most one lime block, and it is the thing to act on now: the live session (Today), the next session (the family's Home), the amount due (Pay), the featured tier (the portal's Enroll page). Offers that sit beside it (turn on reminders, renew for next month) are white cards with a lime icon circle, never a second lime slab.

rules.name: The Club Colors Rule
rules.body: The website wears the club's colors and white, and none of the app's: no Signal Lime, pastels, night tones, or gray canvas. Its colors live only in the `--color-club*` properties, so another academy's colors change values, never components.

rules.name: The Large-on-Green Rule
rules.body: White on Club Green reads about 3.5:1, so Club Green carries white type only at large sizes (24px and up, or 19px and up in bold); smaller lines sit on Deep Green, Jersey Blue, Club Ink, or white. Ball Lime type never sits on Club Green (about 2.5:1): the hero's strip is Deep Green so its lime program names read.

rules.name: The Light Heading Rule
rules.body: Across the app (staff, family portal, wizard, rates sheet), every heading and figure from 22px up is set at weight 300 with slight negative tracking (-0.01em to -0.03em). Bold (700) does not exist in the app; in the app the wordmark (22px, 500) is the only large text that isn't light. The academy website follows its own type rules below.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Every number a coach compares (times, counts, credits, money) is set in tabular lining numerals.

rules.name: The Display Caps Rule
rules.body: On the website, caps belong to the display, secondary, and sticker cuts: names, titles, schedules, prices, numerals, stickers, strips, tabs, the phone menu's rows, and the slanted action, always italic and condensed. Body copy, pills, chips, labels, and inline links stay at normal width in sentence case. Nothing on the website is set in Figtree, and Archivo never appears in the app.

rules.name: The Measured Fit Rule
rules.body: Display words that must fit a width are measured before they render, never after. The hero's name and the "drop soon" stickers are broken into lines by `fitLines` and sized from the display cut's own advance widths (`DISPLAY_EM` in `site-data.ts`, measured from the shipped font files, with the cut's tracking and word spacing); a program's name and times shrink on phones until their longest word fits. New display copy that has to fit is measured the same way before it ships: the table covers A–Z, 0–9, ₱, and common punctuation, and any other glyph counts as an average 0.5em until it is measured and added.

rules.name: The Two-Zone Rule
rules.body: In the app, night tones belong to the command panel and its phone forms (the header block and the tab bar); the canvas, the folder panel, and white cards hold the work. A component that lives in both zones ships two tones, a charcoal tile in the panel and a white card on the canvas, never a dark card on the canvas. The academy website has neither zone: it is built of full-bleed club-color fields (see Academy website).

rules.name: The Thumb Floor Rule
rules.body: Controls start at 44px: buttons and icon circles 44px, fields 48px, check-in toggles and rail circles 48px, a record's action circles 52px. 36px is the one smaller step, for secondary actions inside cards, sheets, bentos, and toasts. A text link set apart from prose (a footer link, a contact line, "All" in a card head) keeps its look and gets an invisible 44px tap area.

rules.name: The Current-in-View Rule
rules.body: A row that scrolls sideways on phones (folder tabs, filter chips, announcement lists) always opens with its current item in view, and a navigation marks exactly one item as current.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: On the website each section is one full-bleed field of one club color, never the color of the field before it, and its edge is that change of color alone: no rules, dividers, or gaps between sections.

rules.name: The What's-Coming Rule
rules.body: A website section with nothing published yet keeps its field and says what's coming, as a fitted two-line sticker with one plain line on what happens next; it never shows blank space, a placeholder graphic, or invented content. How to enroll always shows. Only On court and the team are left out until there are photos and coaches.

rules.name: The Flat Card Rule
rules.body: Cards sit flat; tone alone separates white from gray. A resting element declares its edge once, with a 1px line or a shadow, never both.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Pop means "this floats above the page". Lift is the only other shadow, and only for a thumb or segment raised above its own track. Cards, tiles, and panels never cast one.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: The website has no blur shadows and no gradients: no Pop, Lift, glows, scrims, gradient fills, or gradient text. The halftone is its one gradient-built device, and it is print texture. Depth is drawn with color fields, white die-cut edges, and turns.

rules.name: The Step-Down Radius Rule
rules.body: A shape nested in a container takes a smaller radius than the container: a 32px panel holds 24px list tiles and 22px KPI tiles; a 28px card holds 22px wells and 16px controls.

rules.name: The Slapped-On Rule
rules.body: On the website, stuck-on things sit a few degrees off true, as if slapped on by hand, and neighbors turn opposite ways: stickers between -9° and 8°, photos and portraits within ±3°, package cards and Enroll now's tabs within ±1.5°, strips at -3°. Fields, the nav, the footer, the team page's cards, pills, and body text stay square, and a slanted action's label always stands upright.

rules.name: The Proof Rule
rules.body: A credit count or a balance is a button that opens its proof: the credit ledger or the client's statement.

rules.name: The One Slant Rule
rules.body: On the website the slant belongs to the main move alone: Enroll now, a package's Enroll, Enroll in [program], and, while an academy can't take requests, the hero's "Meet the coaches". Every other action is a plain pill, so the slanted Ball Lime shape always means the one thing to do.

rules.name: The Real Data Rule
rules.body: Every claim, photo, figure, and sticker on the website comes from the academy's own data; the only words the website supplies itself are true for every academy (how enrolling works, what's coming) and, until the academy writes its own line, "Pickleball coaching". A sticker states a fact: that the academy is enrolling now, its lowest price, a coach's DUPR rating or certification, the featured package, a program's lead, a photo's caption, or, on an empty section, what's coming. With nothing to state there is no sticker, and nothing is invented: no testimonials, metrics, slogans, hashtags, or stock photos.

dos: Do split every app screen into the two zones: the night command panel (84px rail and 328px list column on desktop, a black header block on phones) and the gray canvas of white cards.
Do reserve lime (#daee63) for live, selected, and primary: current navigation, the selected tile, action circles, the checked-in toggle, the primary bento.
Do set every pastel and lime fill with ink (#111111) text and icons.
Do set the app's headings and figures from 22px up at weight 300: record titles 44px and page titles 40px from 1024px, both 32px on phones.
Do give every compared number tabular lining numerals (`.num`).
Do open records into folder tabs that fuse into the Folder Gray panel, with the lavender and lime bentos in a 340px column from 1280px.
Do keep controls at 44px or more (fields and check-in toggles 48px, action circles 52px), and use the 36px small button only for secondary actions inside cards, sheets, bentos, and toasts.
Do confirm a check-in with the lime fill, the 220ms settle, and an ink toast that offers Undo.
Do use Lucide icons at 16–24px, with a 1.75 stroke in navigation.
Do show people as initials on a soft wash unless the coach has uploaded a photo.
Do show an academy's logo as uploaded, on a white tile, and in the app keep the CoachMan palette around it unchanged.
Do spend lime once per screen in the family portal (the next session, the amount due); make offers white cards with a lime icon circle.

Do keep the academy website's way in on its first phone screen: the slanted Ball Lime Enroll now in the nav and the hero while the academy takes requests, else Message us (and, in the hero, Meet the coaches).

Do introduce people on the public pages with 4:5 half-body portraits (else the square photo, else initials on a soft wash), the name and title beside or under the image, never on it. On phones a coach's own card leads with a full-width portrait and the rest of the team scrolls sideways; faces in a stack stay circles.

Do keep a visible keyboard focus ring on every control and link: in the app, ink on the canvas and lime in the dark zone; on the website, a 3px ring at 3px offset, ink on the white and Ball Lime fields and Ball Lime on Deep Green, Jersey Blue, and Club Ink.
Do give a text link set apart from prose a 44px tap area, and open a sideways-scrolling row with its current item in view.

Do build the academy website from full-bleed fields of the club's colors, one per section and never the color of the field before it: Club Green with its halftone, Jersey Blue, Deep Green, Ball Lime, white, and a Club Ink footer.

Do set the website's names, titles, schedules, prices, stickers, strips, tabs, and slanted actions in Archivo's condensed italic caps (the display cut at 62% width and 900: the hero's name fitted up to 168px, section titles 96px from 1024px), and everything else in Archivo at normal width, in sentence case.

Do build every website section from the academy's own data. A section with nothing yet keeps its field and says what's coming as a fitted sticker with one line beside it; How to enroll always shows; On court and the team wait for photos and coaches.
Do measure display words that must fit before they render (`fitLines` and `DISPLAY_EM` in `site-data.ts`), and measure any glyph the table lacks before a fitted line uses it.

Do keep the website's motion to three things: the hero's stickers slapping on once as the page opens (560ms, starting 140, 260, and 380ms in), the team page's program swap, and the phone's contact bar sliding in. With reduced motion none of it animates: the stickers are simply there and the swap is instant.
donts: Don't use lime to mark a category, a tag, or a chart series; categories take the pastels.
